content:
Hi everyone! Me & @Anton Kovsharov are happy to announce the beta version of the Paperproof vscode extension (github.com/Paper-Proof/paperproof), a new proof interface for Lean 4 that's supposed to feel like pen-and-paper proofs.

When we're inspecting a proof in Lean, we see a list of tactics - commands that change hypothesis/goal types. In vscode's Infoview, we can see hypothesis/goal types at any given moment, but we never get to see the full picture of how these types were changing throughout the proof - that's left to our mind's eye.
Paperproof takes this proof tree out of our imagination and onto paper, making the full structure of the proof apparent.

In other words - Paperproof switches the focus from verbs (tactics) to nouns (types). With tactics, we're seeing a list of directions - with Paperproof, we're seeing a map with arrows on it. This is easier shown than told, so below we're including a Paperproof screencast and a number of fully-rendered proofs from Mathlib and other repos.

Here is a video of Paperproof in action:

And this is how Paperproof renders proofs from some well-known repos:

  • Mathlib

  • Mathematics in Lean (Jeremy Avigad, Patrick Massot)

  • Hitchhiker's Guide to Logical Verification (Anne Baanen, Alexander Bentkamp, Jasmin Blanchette, Johannes Hölzl, Jannis Limperg)

There are a few edge cases we're still working on - currently we only render tactic-based proofs (those that start with by), and some proofs in Mathlib can be hard to zoom into; however it should work in most cases.
We'll be happy if you try it, and feel free to get back at us with any questions, feature requests and bug reports.

PS - special thanks to @Wojciech Nawrocki & @Edward Ayers for advice and support during Paperproof development.
